metadata.title: Delta, Every Feature, Played
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-waikthrough walker film. Every gameplay beat is an exact-frame window of a scripted-input take of the real game; no human playtest. Game audio was not captured; narration only. No paid calls, no upload. Vertical companion: designed beats re-rendered as native 9:16 cards or 916 compositions; gameplay re-cut in portrait from the same frames.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. This is how Walker is meant to be asked: a game design document in, a playable Godot project out. The prompt is a reconstruction. This game was a Unity first-person puzzle game with scripts and art but no levels, rebuilt in Godot with twelve.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a first-person puzzle game — a space station folded into two layers, energy cells carried between machines, and an unstable core taken past two guardians — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: 12 levels, 2 station layers, 27 scripts and 3 shaders.
Played here: 4 scripted-input takes, 90 of 90 assertions passing.

beats.narration_text: Delta is a first-person puzzle game. A space station folded into two layers, fifty metres apart, and you shift between them carrying energy cells. Every feature here is played through real keyboard, mouse and gamepad input, by a script. Nobody has played it by hand yet.

props.text:
Delta
is a space shooter.
Twelve levels, two layers.

beats.narration_text: Level twelve, Delta. Two guardians, one in each layer, attack the layer you're in every twenty seconds. This is a strike: red sparks follow you for five seconds, then lock in place, and lightning hits that spot three seconds later. The warning says get clear, and the script does, by more than the three metre radius.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. All twelve levels, the ending, the failures and the other inputs play through real input, and ninety assertions pass. Two defects in the pause menu: mouse clicks don't reach it, and R and N don't work while paused. And standing still, you creep ahead on a moving shuttle. Whether the puzzles are fair, or fun, is a person's call.
